boundary_evidence: One contiguous run of the 2D engines' BG base-address getters, 0x02054d38..0x020551f0: for each of BG0..BG3 the screen-base and character-base getter of the main engine (G2) and the sub engine (G2S), sixteen functions with no gaps.
Each G2S getter sits directly below its G2 twin (BG0 screen at the top through BG3 character at the bottom), the pairing the Nitro SDK's gx_bgcnt source file uses.
Vram__Map (0x02054c80..0x02054d38) below is a VRAM-bank mapper and func_020551f0 above has a different shape; neither calls into or is called by the getter set.
No data, bss or RTTI: the getters read fixed I/O registers and return computed addresses, so nothing but the sixteen functions emits.
notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows arm9/G2x.
G2 and G2S are Nitro SDK namespaces with no header; the TU declares both in its preamble. It does not include decl_common.h, whose `extern int G2[];` hides `namespace G2`.

func_02054d88, func_02054ea8 and func_02054efc are G2's BG3, BG1 and BG0 character getters. They keep their address names under extern "C" because their callers name them that way; renaming them to G2::GetBG*CharPtr is a separate change across those callers.
The file is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order; the emitted object carries the sixteen functions ascending 0x02054d38..0x020551f0.
